Dali creates his most haunting allegory of the empty space in which time is at an end.
The barren landscape, without horizon, drifts to infinity, lit by some eerie, never setting sun.
An amorphous creature sleeps in the foreground, draped with a limp watch.
Another such watch hangs from the branch of a dead tree; yet another hangs half over the edge of a rectangular form.
The watches are visible by ants and a fly, as if they were decaying, organic life, soft and viscous.
The watch- a metallic, intricate, and precise instrument – is metamorphosed into an object devourable by busy ants.
We recognize the impossible landscape and its impossibe contents as perfectly possible in the dream world.
